claims.text: The initial material is cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility.
Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
Untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr has poor oxygen resistance near 1000 °C in air, resulting in detrimental oxidation.
HfNbTaTiZr high-entropy-alloy material can be fabricated into electrodes and used to produce a coating by electrospark deposition.
Electrospark deposition can apply the proposed coating directly onto cast HfNbTaTiZr.
The electrospark-deposited coating will be thin and adherent on the HfNbTaTiZr substrate.
An oxidation-resistant variant of the HfNbTaTiZr coating formulation could be used.
The deposited coating will form or facilitate a dense, adherent, stable refractory oxide scale at 1000 °C in air.
The oxide scale will act as a diffusion barrier that retards oxygen transport into the underlying alloy.
Retarding oxygen diffusion will minimize continued oxidation during high-temperature service.
After 100 hours at 1000 °C in air, coated specimens will have markedly lower oxygen uptake and surface oxidation than uncoated controls.
The coating will preserve the alloy's original room-temperature tensile ductility after high-temperature exposure.
The coating will preserve the alloy's original yield strength at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
The proposed protection is expected to remain effective while the material is mechanically loaded at strain rates of 10^-4–10^-2 s^-1.
